dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: We're counting on you to wrap this match up fast... But this challenge's a little different, so keep your guard up.

choices.text: Then let's do this.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Easy there. No need to go all out and bring the whole Domain down.

choices.text: What are you doing between matches?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I'm treating Iris to a couple drinks. She got me these sunglasses in Fontaine, so I owe her.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: ...Hey, don't give me that look.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I'll be in Snezhnaya for a while, so I'd better get used to warming up with the local Fire-Water. I'm taking a quick break first.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I should ask Iris for tips, too. She's been on Dragonspine for years. She probably knows enough about handling the cold to write a whole book series.

choices.text: About commissions and Adventurer Rank...

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Hm? What brought this up?

choices.text: I never really thought about commission ranks before.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: No need to think too hard about it. It's just a rough way to describe what kind of commissions an adventurer can handle alone.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I'm guessing you want to know where the commissions we usually give you fall, right?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: A hilichurl outpost raid is a good example. Adventurers call those "Increasing Danger," and they're usually treated as B-rank commissions.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: For that kind of job, the Guild recommends at least sixteen regular adventurers and warriors, with no fewer than six solid marksmen.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: The usual plan is to have six people keep any Mitachurls in the outpost busy, while four handle the regular hilichurls.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: The six marksmen take out the Hilichurl Crossbowmen on the towers first, then help wear down the Mitachurls. Once they're down, the whole party moves in to clear the camp.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: That can take three to five hours, so it's more about endurance than brute force.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: If possible, bring a cook with the party so everyone can recover after the fight and be ready if hilichurl reinforcements show up.

choices.text: It doesn't seem that complicated to me...

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Right, and that's why you shouldn't get too hung up on the rating. By today's standards, it's pretty broad.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Iris's said the same thing before. A B-rank hilichurl camp in Dragonspine and a B-rank "Increasing Danger" commission in a normal area aren't really the same at all.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: We're suggesting that each rank should also have a difficulty score. For example, B-rank would be 601 to 700 points. That way, adventurers can get a better idea of how hard a commission is before they take it.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: There'll be a meeting about it after the event ends, so you'll hear more then.

choices.text: I usually just go in and get it done...
I heard something about adventurer ranks this time.
I've fought my way through enough by now. I'm not scared.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Heh, fair enough. A fight on paper's still a fight. Go on, then. Let's see what you've got, all-rounder.

dialogues.speaker: Liliuo
dialogues.text: Well, look who's joining in! If our dazzling "Tumaini" is competing too, the leaderboard might not know what hit it. I'd better be careful, or I'll be the first one knocked off...

choices.text: I'll go first for the puzzle challenge.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: Puzzles aren't really my strong suit, so I'll watch and pick up a thing or two from you.

choices.text: You look kind of familiar...

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: Oh, so I was that forgettable...

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: It was the last Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame. Your student, Kachina, beat me in the competition.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: And lately, every time I see her, she's all, "I heard Master's gotten even stronger overseas..."

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: Courage is admirable. But knowing when you're outmatched is just as important. There's no glory in challenging someone you can't even hope to reach.

choices.text: You met Kachina?

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: Whoa, easy there, Lord Tumaini.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: We just bumped into each other at the Chuwen Fair, so I bought her a meal. I didn't exactly abduct her!

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: And for the record, losing once doesn't mean I'm going to run around picking fights with people. A real tribal warrior has more pride than that.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: And anyway, Kachina's teaching me the Children of Echoes' dance steps. I've got nothing but respect for her now.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: If I was up to anything shady, may the Pyro Archon cut me down right here and send me to kneel before Atea forever.

choices.text: What did you do to Kachina?
That's pretty modest for a veteran.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: A real veteran knows how to size up a fight and when to back off.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: Back then, I thought I had it all figured out — more years under my belt, better gear, a bit more experience. So I looked down on younger opponents.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: Then Kachina knocked me down a peg. I was so embarrassed I could barely face anyone afterward. It took me a long time to get over it...

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: In that entire great battle, I only took out around three hundred Abyss monsters. I was ashamed of myself.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: Afterward, Granny Itztli really let me have it, and that finally got me back on my feet. I started taking combat commissions from the Adventurers' Guild, working myself back into fighting shape, and brushing up on everything I'd fallen behind on...

choices.text: But you're an S-rank adventurer now...

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: Well, it's not that simple. Adventuring takes a whole range of skills. It's different from front-line combat in more ways than you'd think.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: Lately, I've been teaching the younger adventurers at the Guild some of my combat techniques. In return, they've been teaching me all kinds of useful tips for everyday life and exploration.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: With people like Miss Valerina helping me, I was even able to track down those old music scores Rilai and Sappho had wanted for so long...

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: They really made me realize something: every generation has its share of talented young people. Some of them are real gems.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: If the younger generation can learn from our experience — and our mistakes — then of course they're going to go further than we did.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: And Kachina? She's got you as her teacher, and all those Ancient Name bearers influencing her along the way...

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: A few years from now, she may be standing so high that even I'll have to look up to her.

choices.text: Sounds like you did more than just "brush up"...
Then I'd better take this competition seriously and give it my best.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: That's the spirit. Kachina really drove that lesson home for me. No matter how long you've been doing this, or how one-sided the match looks, you should always start by respecting your opponent.

dialogues.speaker: Rika
dialogues.text: Oh, hey there! Looks like we're both in the competition. Are you here to pick up Yae Publishing House's latest novel, or do you want to jump right into the train simulation?

choices.text: Let's do the train simulation first.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: I'd only ever read about trains in light novels before. Hope you have fun too!

choices.text: Why are you selling novels? Aren't you an adventurer?

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: What, adventurers aren't allowed to sell things? I'm not the only one who does a little work on the side, you know...

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Adventuring gets expensive fast. Every commission, I burn through elemental potions and all kinds of other supplies. Then I get my reward, add everything up, and somehow I'm still out a few hundred thousand Mora.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: So what else can I do? Pick up some extra work, sell a few things here and there, and help pay the bills...

choices.text: Then why keep adventuring if it's such a money sink...?

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Absolutely not. A steady, by-the-book life? I'd be bored out of my skull before the week was over.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: What I want is to wake up somewhere new every day, meet people I've never met, see things I've never seen, and take on challenges I've never faced before.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: And for me, being an adventurer is the only way to live it.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Honestly, this competition has already been more than worth it. I've made friends from all over, and I've seen so many incredible things here in the land of ice and snow.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Too bad I'm hopeless at writing.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: I'll have to ask one of the editors to help me put together a letter for Souka, our resident deadline dodger. I'll tell her about everything I've seen lately, and maybe she can use some of it for her stories...

choices.text: If Mora's that tight, maybe you should get a regular job...
Um... your ears...

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Oh, they're fake! Just props. Same goes for the shrine maiden costume.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: A few years back, I took on an S-rank commission, which left me with way too much debt. After trying this and that, I somehow ended up working part-time at Yae Publishing House.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Then my luck turned around. The Irodori Festival was in full swing, so I got dressed up as a novel character and helped promote some collaboration drinks...

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: The promotion actually went really well. Aratani was happy with how I did, and I even got a nice bonus out of it.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: So ever since then, I've been working myself to the bone for Yae Publishing House. It's the steadiest job I've got.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Not that I'm stuck behind a counter or anything, though. I still spend most of my time traveling, camping, and adventuring all over the place.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: And when I meet people on the road, I recommend light novels that fit the mood. That's where most of my sales come from!

choices.text: Maybe next time.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Huh? Oh, alright... Well, if you ever get bored, come buy a book from me!

dialogues.speaker: Nadia
dialogues.text: I feel like I've seen you before... Here for the shooting contest?

choices.text: Then let's begin.

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: You've got the hands for a musket. I bet you'll put on a good show.

choices.text: We've met before, actually.

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: Really? Was it in Fontaine?

choices.text: Somewhere you'll remember sooner or later.

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: Then I'm sure it'll come back to me soon enough.

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: Urville's been working really hard lately. He's done so many commissions, found some amazing treasure, and made a lot of money.

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: He says he's going to find me the best doctor there is, so I can get better at remembering things.

choices.text: By the Rusty Rudder.

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: That's right! Now I remember. You helped us a lot back then. Next time, I won't take so long to recognize you.

choices.text: Have we met before?

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: Maybe not, but now we have.

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: You make me feel really, really good about things. I feel like if I stay with you, something nice will happen.

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: If you ever come to Fontaine, you should visit the Rusty Rudder.

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: I'll make you some Tidalga Conch Brew. I made it a few months ago, and I wrote everything down, so I won't forget how.

choices.text: So, you're competing too, Melusine?

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: Yes. I'm going to try really hard.

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: Someone said Urville and I make a great team, so they asked us to represent them. They gave us lots of money, and a book to help us know what to say.

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: So I think entering the contest is a good thing.

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: I haven't used these muskets before, but the idea is the same. Once I'm holding one, I can use it.

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: I just wish it weren't so cold. Even one little breath makes everything fog up...

choices.text: Make sure you get some rest.

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: I will. I sleep ten hours a day.

dialogues.speaker: Urville
dialogues.text: These people are hard to beat. Professional adventurers really are something else. Every one of them has five or six tricks up their sleeve.

choices.text: That's not how the saying goes in Liyue.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: I know how it goes, but... these contestants are way stronger than normal. It's fine to exaggerate a little, right?

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: Besides, if we're talking about Nadia, I'd say she's got ten tricks up her sleeve.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: In a shooting match, I don't think anyone can beat her.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: The only person who might have a tiny edge is that Snezhnayan clerk, and only because he knows this model of musket better than she does.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: Once I find the best doctor out there and Nadia stops forgetting things so much, she'll be able to show everyone what she's really capable of...

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: Then we'll make a fortune, save up enough Mora in a year or two, and we won't have to work so hard every day anymore.

choices.text: Are you a contestant too?

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: Well, not exactly. I'm accompanying Nadia, Fontaine's S-rank adventurer. Officially, I'm registered as her strategist.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: After that treasure hunt where we saved that famous adventurer-diver, the commissions started coming in one after another.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: Then Nadia somehow managed to catch some runaway thing called... "Legris, the Faux-Holy Sword," I think.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: I don't really know the details, but apparently it's a super rare Hat Jellyfish, and almost no diver can beat it.

choices.text: I remember that. It is pretty tough.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: Even you think so? Then I guess that explains it...

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: Ever since then, this adventurer named Ophelia keeps bringing Nadia jobs that "no normal person could handle."

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: But Nadia clears them every time without breaking a sweat. I'm only there watching, and even I never feel nervous.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: After that, Nadia got a new reputation: an adventurer who could take on S-rank commissions. I got a bit of credit too, just for being with her.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: Ophelia is paying for our trip to Snezhnaya this time, and she gave me some "negotiation principles" too — a list of the things the Fontaine branch really cares about.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: In the meeting earlier, I followed those points and argued our side. It seemed to go pretty well, all things considered.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: And if Nadia and I can pull this off, there's even a bonus waiting for us back home.

choices.text: That's great.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: Yeah... But somehow, I can't help feeling like this isn't right.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: I should be working harder and making more Mora, so Nadia can take it easy and live more comfortably.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: Anyway, there are a lot of strong-looking people here in Snezhnaya. I'm going to ask them for some training tips...

choices.text: Congratulations.
Never heard of it, but with a name that long, it's probably strong.
You've got this.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: Ah... Thank you. I won't give up.

dialogues.speaker: NPC#17331
dialogues.text: #Hello, {NICKNAME}. Thank you again for taking part in the first Adventurers' Tournament.

choices.text: Could you remind me who you are?

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: Ah... To be honest, what I said when we first met was just about everything...

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: My name is Talalikhin Gogol. I serve as a clerk at Adventurers' Guild Headquarters.

choices.text: But your leaderboard score is not low by any means.

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: I was only asked to take part because I'm familiar with this kind of work. The rest was just luck

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: Besides, I suppose I did have a bit of an advantage — Snezhnayan adventurers are more used to contest events like these, after all.

choices.text: Is that really the sort of ranking one would expect from a clerk?
Are you close with Lan?

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: I would not say close, exactly. She has been with the Guild much longer than I have.

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: But this time, Lan and I will be working together behind the scenes.

choices.text: What do you mean?

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: Do you remember the sword called "Unseen Razor"?

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: Lan, the Liyue Branch Master of the Adventurers' Guild, is also Huo Lanling — the "Swordseeker of Qingxu." She has never failed a commission since taking office.

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: There is another important reason Lan came here. She is searching for the former owner of "Unseen Razor."

choices.text: I don't know much about what happened with Lan...

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: In that case, if you do not mind, I can take a few minutes to explain.

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: Lan and I both have a reason to find this person.

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: Because...

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: Her elder brother, Master Huo Zhaohui, once traveled across the frozen plains of Snezhnaya alongside my uncle.

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: They were searching for the "adamant material," hoping to forge the perfect blade and develop a fighting style where warrior and weapon moved as one.

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: But in the end, they were both caught up in an accident involving the Shadow Realm, and no one has known where they are ever since.

choices.text: I had not heard of this before...

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: That is understandable. The accident was extremely complicated, and the investigation report alone was thicker than a dictionary.

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: The full report was only thoroughly reviewed recently, and the information in it was confirmed to be "relatively accurate." The Special Assignments Battalion has since shared it with the Adventurers' Guild.

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: Once the tournament is over, I will be organizing those findings on the Guild's behalf and using them to create a set of mental training exercises based on simulated Shadow Realm combat.

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: If you are interested, you can find me near the headquarters then.

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: For the sake of the Guild, and for personal reasons as well, I will do everything I can to help Lan find her brother.

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: Perhaps I may also have a chance to find my uncle and help my family move past the grief we have carried for years.

choices.text: Did Lan not know about it?
I think I helped her look for that sword before...

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: Then you do remember. She mentioned it recently, how the two of you searched for the sword together. She seemed very excited when she spoke of it.

choices.text: Are you two working together on something else?
This must be hard for you, too.

response.speaker: NPC#17331
response.text: Thank you for your concern. This is my duty, and I will do my best.

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: Cold... It's certainly cold. If I had known it would be like this, I would have brought Cyrus along and had him put in some extra training.

choices.text: Colder than Dragonspine?

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: The nature of it is different.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: Fruit wine can reach the same strength as Fire-Water after multiple distillations, but the way it affects you is not something that can be measured by strength alone.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: In the past, I would have told you that if you wanted to go into Dragonspine, you needed to make sure you were fully prepared.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: Do you see the key point there? "Go into Dragonspine."

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: That is the dividing line. Up until that moment, you still have time to breathe, time to get everything ready, and above all, time to prepare yourself mentally.

choices.text: Now that you mention it, I guess that's true.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: But Snezhnaya is different. From the moment you set foot here, you can no longer escape that cold. Instead, it surrounds you every minute, every second.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: It is a trial for both body and mind.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: Think of it this way. In Mondstadt, strong drink is something people have after work. However hard the liquor is to swallow, and however dull the company you end up with may be, you can grit your teeth and get through it.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: But in Snezhnaya, it is as though everyone has Fire-Water mixed into their drinking water. No matter what you drink, it leaves you dizzy.

choices.text: That's an interesting comparison.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: No... wait. Someone actually did that.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: When I first arrived in Morepesok and stopped for a meal, there really was Fire-Water in the drinking water...

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: Did they mix it up by mistake, or is that genuinely their way of treating guests?

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: No, I should not think about it any further... A serious lapse in judgment! I really should have dragged Cyrus along and put him through some proper hard training.

choices.text: That's kind of a terrifying comparison.
I never really thought about it that way...
How's the competition looking?

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: Well... I'm not as young as I used to be. I can't really keep up anymore.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: So now it all depends on how Little Huo does in the end.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: Of course, she's not quite on your level. But based on all the intel Alfry has put together, she should have a real shot at second place.

choices.text: Little... H—Huo?

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: Oh, I mean Lan. You know her as Lan, don't you? I'm ten years...

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: Well, a few years older than her, so it would feel strange for me to call her that so formally. Little Huo works well enough. Or Little Lan, I suppose.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: When she first came to Mondstadt, she looked every bit as young as you do now.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: Margaret was still a reckless young girl back then as well. She once mixed up an order and got quite the scolding from the owner.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: Margaret burst into tears and said, "One day, I'm going to be a boss too, and then I can scold anyone I want!"

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: Little Lan was right beside her, cheering her on: "Then when I become a famous adventurer, I'll bring lots and lots of friends from Liyue to give you plenty of business!"

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: In the end, Margaret really did become a tavern owner. And even now, she is still as bright as ever.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: But Little Lan... after her brother went missing, I never saw her smile like that again.

choices.text: Sounds like the two of you really go back a long way.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: I suppose we do. We do not see each other much in everyday life, but every six months or so, whenever we finally meet, we talk about anything and everything, and drink until we lose track of time...

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: Ahem. I think we have wandered a little too far from the point. Let us stop there for now...

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: In any case, since coming to Snezhnaya, Little Lan has seemed surprisingly upbeat.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: I do not know what good thing happened to her, but I hope her good luck continues.

choices.text: So Lan is actually getting on a bit herself, then.
Wait... who?
I'm all for that.

response.speaker: Iris
response.text: Right? Then next time you go to the Mondstadt branch, just knock him out and carry him over here. Tell them I said it was fine.

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: This is quite the sight. Skilled adventurers from every branch, all gathered in one place... It feels like something out of a rousing action film.

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: If the rules were a little less restrictive and there were more chances to spar, this competition would be just about perfect.

choices.text: Maybe, but adventurers need more than combat skills.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: I agree. Adventuring is not simply a matter of fighting. It also requires stamina for long journeys, scouting and search skills, wilderness survival, the ability to handle unfavorable battles, and the judgment to read a changing situation.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: Combat alone does not make one a qualified adventurer.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: However, an adventurer who cannot fight at all presents a serious liability. They become the weak point in the party's formation. Monsters and criminals are quick to exploit such openings. And if that happens, the whole team could be wiped out.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: Being weak for now isn't the problem. With enough training, you can improve. The real problem is using "teamwork" as an excuse not to try. That is the worst kind of attitude.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: At the very least, here at the Nod-Krai branch, I intend to keep adventurers like that to a minimum.

choices.text: So wouldn't that make you the weak link too?

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: Oh? You saw me using a heavy crossbow before, did you?

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: Then you caught me at a rather embarrassing time...

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: Still, I do improve. Thanks to Mr. Talalikhin, I can handle the grenadiers' weapons quite well now.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: Of course, against someone on the "Swordseeker of Qingxu's" level, I doubt I'd last a single hit.

choices.text: That title sounds familiar.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: You've known her for a while, haven't you? She's the Liyue Branch Master — the swordswoman people call Lan.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: Her first S-rank commission came when she was only eight jobs into her career. It took place near Qingxu Pool, where she defeated a Stonehide Lawachurl.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: When the fight was over, she had suffered about seventy wounds and fractures, along with severe blood loss. Even so, she made it back to camp by herself and held out until reinforcements arrived.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: People asked if she had lost her mind, going into a Stonehide Lawachurl's territory alone.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: She said she didn't know — she simply hadn't thought about it that much. All she cared about was finding the sword.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: The way she treated her own wounds in the field was later written up by the Adventurers' Guild and added to some of their reference materials.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: When I first heard about it, I was just a troublesome little kid, always pestering my mother for Midsommar Torte. I thought it was just another fairy tale...

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: But before I had even talked her into giving me ten tortes, the story had already continued... The "Swordseeker of Qingxu" was back on her feet in no time, and then went straight on to complete her second S-rank commission...

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: She really is something else... I suppose only people who have been with the Guild for over ten years still remember how much that title shook everyone back then.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: When Lan signed up for the competition, she actually went by "No-Frills Instant Kill." But some of the old-timers recognized her right away, so in the end, she used the classic title after all.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: Before she leaves Snezhnaya, I'll have to catch her and ask if she'd be willing to advise the Nod-Krai branch for a while.

choices.text: Why do they call her that again?
I think it's pretty interesting, too.

response.speaker: Sarin
response.text: Then let's enjoy the rest of the event.

dialogues.speaker: Valerina
dialogues.text: Ah, we meet again, Honorary Knight, Cat Savior. I've entered as an adventurer from Mondstadt myself.

dialogues.speaker: Valerina
dialogues.text: A little unexpected, yes. I had gone back to Natlan to visit some friends, but it just so happened that they were leaving on a trip. And since I was already there, they brought me along...

choices.text: How have you been lately?

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: Everything's been going quite smoothly.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: A little while ago, Mr. Bennett took a few of the Guild veterans to Easybreeze Holiday Resort in Natlan, and they had a wonderful time there.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: They all spoke so highly of the place that I decided to visit it myself. And goodness, it was every bit as relaxing as they said...

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: And then, on the eighth day of my vacation, I happened to spot Miss Liliuo sunbathing on the beach with two close friends of hers.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: From what I heard, one is called "Sappho Amidst the Waves," and the other is Rilai, the "Frozen Collar."

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: Liliuo does the singing for the group, and she plays the Djem Djem Drum too. Sometimes she'll even bring out a cajon — one of those box drums you sit on while you play.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: Sappho usually plays the ukulele, but she can play a full-sized classical guitar as well. That guitar of hers even has Master Dvorak's signature on it.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: Rilai is a flutist, but she can also play the Nightwind Horn. She just chooses whichever instrument fits the sound they need, and she does it so effortlessly. Honestly, I doubt there's any song she couldn't play.

choices.text: They sound like such kind people...

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: They're kind and impressive, and somehow, animals love them just as much! I followed them on a weeklong journey of fruit wine and music, listened to my heart's content, and had a wonderful time...

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: After that, they pulled me into the group, and we all set out to find a lost score.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: We'd only found it a day or two earlier when Miss Liliuo received the invitation to this tournament. She decided on the spot that I was coming with her, too.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: They seemed to be looking to some older pieces for inspiration, hoping it would help them perfect their new song.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: They did gain something from the search in the end, though I expect it will still take them some time to finish writing the song.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: But that only makes me look forward to it all the more. I can hardly wait. I suppose I'll just have to visit them in Natlan every couple of months from now on!

choices.text: They sound really impressive...
Actually, I don't remember who you are.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: Huh? How could you say that!?

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: Oh well... I guess that means I didn't stand out enough. I'll just have to send you a little gift from time to time, so you don't forget me again.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: In that case, allow me to introduce myself properly. I'm Valerina — riddle solver and caretaker of the Furball Fortress.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: More recently, I've also invested in Dodoco's Blow-Up-Erative Bomb-Nanza, a tabletop game series designed by Lisa and Miss Ematol...

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: If you ever have a project that needs funding, and you think it has solid business potential, you're welcome to show me the proposal. I can invest quite a bit of Mora!

choices.text: That's great. Then let's both do our best.

response.speaker: Valerina
response.text: Yes! I've done rather well this time, actually. I've already managed to place higher than expected in the non-combat events, so I'm more than satisfied.

dialogues.speaker: Lemta
dialogues.text: Things are still such a mess... I didn't do that well in the competition either. It feels like my bad luck's spilling over like pilaf from an overfilled pot...

choices.text: Having some trouble?

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: Ah, perfect timing. An expert, just when I needed one.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: What do you think of my hairstyle?

choices.text: It's... pretty classic?

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: That's a very polite way to put it. You're too kind.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: A while ago, when I was passing through Fontaine, Ophelia kept raving about her hairstylist, so I went and got myself a "fashionable new look."

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: In Sumeru, only the wealthier ladies can call in a real expert and spend hours getting a style like this done.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: It was only afterward that I realized this hairstyle doesn't go with my face or my outfit at all... I really regret it.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: Once I'm back in Sumeru City, I'll have to figure out how to change myself back. Otherwise, Avena is definitely going to tease me about it.

choices.text: Ophelia?

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: She's an incredible adventurer. She manages all the supplies for the entire Fontaine branch of the Adventurers' Guild.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: Back when we were exploring the desert, there was a misunderstanding between her and the mercenary company I was with at the time. Things got out of hand, and she ended up taking down seven of us.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: Later, Lady Candace stepped in and smoothed things over. Ophelia actually covered an entire year's worth of water expenses for us. An entire year!

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: That's the kind of money we would usually spend three months earning. If anything, she was a little too sincere.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: The sad thing is, I heard she was badly injured when some out-of-control experimental field-force device came crashing down on her. She did recover, but she couldn't really stay on the front lines afterward.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: Otherwise, she'd probably be competing here too.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: Next time there's an event like this, maybe I'll bring her along to watch.

choices.text: Avena?

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: A sweet, innocent young lady. She's my employer — the one I'm here to protect.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: She chose me as her bodyguard because she said we "just clicked" when we met, and promised to introduce me to some amazing adventurers.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: As it turned out, they were all bright-eyed rookies with big dreams, kind hearts, and no idea how dangerous the world can be. Some of them even had mentors I'd beaten before.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: She funds the entire team without expecting anything in return... She's almost unbelievably generous, in that innocent way of hers.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: That's why I don't mind tagging along and carrying her bags. I want to see this team grow into something...

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: ...Provided she doesn't empty her purse first. She needs someone to help her judge what's worth the money, so I'll keep an eye on her.

choices.text: It doesn't really suit you, somehow.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: Right? That's because I never used to wear my hair like this.

choices.text: Have we met before?

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: ...Perhaps. If you've ever turned in commissions at the Adventurers' Guild in Sumeru City, you might have seen me there with my employer.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: Over the years, my employer and I would often stop there to rest after buying supplies.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: I usually ended up taking care of certain commissions for her... ones she never quite realized were as difficult as they were.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: So Branch Master Kamal gave me a part-time adventurer's certificate as well. It's worked out rather well — I can earn a little extra Mora that way.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: If he hadn't suddenly decided on a whim to spend his vacation out at sea, he would have been the one leading Sumeru's team.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: He's rather carefree, really. Since I've helped him more than forty times already, he even felt comfortable leaving meetings like this to me. I can hardly let him down now, can I?

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: Mm, I seem to have gotten a little off topic...

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: Anyway, if we ever get the chance, we should work together. My employer is rather generous, you know.

choices.text: Then here's hoping your luck changes for the better today.

response.speaker: Lemta
response.text: Thank you. I hope the same for you.

dialogues.speaker: Sukhrab
dialogues.text: The Shock-Boiling Device is in good condition. Its restraint components should be able to withstand another nineteen days of high-intensity operation... That will be sufficient.

choices.text: What are you muttering about?

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: Interested? This is an alchemical mechanism known as the Shock-Boiling Device, designed to greatly enhance one's combat capabilities.

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: As long as you possess a certain degree of fighting ability to begin with, it can bring out combat power on par with a seasoned veteran.

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: And if you, like me, have tempered yourself through rigorous training and battle, then once you use it, you'll be able to perform at one hundred and twenty percent in every fight.

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: Sounds good, doesn't it? You can place an order with me now. Once I return to Sumeru, I'll let Professor Hajanad know, and she can arrange for the workshop to fit your order into the schedule.

choices.text: That name sounds familiar...

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: That's only natural. The Professor once said the device was created with "the help of the most brilliant person in the world," and that the experience felt "like two of the most wonderful dreams."

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: As the Akademiya gradually comes to recognize her academic achievements, I'm sure her story will reach more and more people.

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: And once her work earns the recognition it deserves, she'll be able to help even more people with that kind heart of hers...

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: ...If only her silly grin weren't so terrifying, she'd be perfect.

choices.text: I don't know what it is, and I'm not interested.

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: Then you're passing up something valuable. Even the Corps of Thirty has started equipping a small number of its members with the Shock-Boiling Device, you know.

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: I'm sure Professor Hajanad will keep improving it until it's as affordable and reliable as a scimitar — a piece of support equipment that can help protect Sumeru even better.

choices.text: You're from Sumeru?

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: That's right. Didn't think you'd be able to tell at a glance.

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: I used to live north of Port Ormos, making my living as a hunter. Back then, I hadn't seen much of the world...

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: Then I was fortunate enough to take on a temporary commission, escorting some scholars through an area crowded with Fungi while they carried out their research. That was when Professor Hajanad noticed me, and invited me to study under her at the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: That was how I came to assist with her research and take on all kinds of adventuring commissions.

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: And now, with the Shock-Boiling Device's help, I've completed 137 A-rank commissions.

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: I may not have any extraordinary achievements, like clearing an S-rank commission, but I've always made up for it with diligence. That's how I earned the Guild's recommendation and came here to compete with Captain Lemta's team.

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: I just hope my final results will make the Professor proud...

choices.text: Please excuse me now...

response.speaker: Sukhrab
response.text: Oh? Well... until next time, then?

dialogues.speaker: Match Commentator
dialogues.text: Ah... Seeing this many incredible adventurers compete on the same stage makes even overtime feel worth it...

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Everything on the Guild's end has been taken care of. Next, we're headed to... hmm, the icefield north of Svetloledovka.

choices.text: I still want to go over that battle again...

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Sure. Let's have one more good fight.

choices.text: Do you have more work to do?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: It's no big deal. Talalikhin and I are just going to look into a few... leads.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: You've already helped us more than enough. I won't trouble you again this time.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: With a local showing us around, it'll be as easy as sightseeing.

choices.text: Best wishes to you.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Mm-hmm. I've got a feeling luck's on all our sides.

dialogues.speaker: Liliuo
dialogues.text: I lost to you, just like everyone expected. At this rate, you've probably won so many trophies that not even a Long-Necked Rhino could carry them all...

choices.text: I'd like to go over the puzzle challenge one more time.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: Sure. It'll be a good refresher for me, too.

choices.text: So, what's next for you?

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: It's just too cold here. Even someone from the Masters of the Night-Wind like me can barely take it. I'll probably stay for another two weeks at most.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: Once I'm back home, I'm going to tell Rilai and Sappho all about the interesting things I've seen here.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: Oh, and that incredible bartender's creations... I wonder if she does takeout?

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: Oh, right! I'm also planning to bring Grandma and Kachina the most expensive desserts in Snezhnaya. And I'll be sure to tell them all about your unbelievable performance here, too.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: Of course, if you'd rather keep a low profile, or tell them yourself... I won't say a word.

choices.text: Not quite. I'll count them when I get back.

response.speaker: Liliuo
response.text: Then be sure to let me know the next time we meet!

dialogues.speaker: Rika
dialogues.text: Ugh... overall results are barely acceptable, I guess. But when I total up the gains and expenses this time, things don't look great...

choices.text: I want to go over the train simulation again.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Go over it? Sure, sure! We can start right away.

choices.text: I'll leave you to it, then.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Take care on your way back. I still need to settle the accounts...

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Oh no... why does it look like I'm going to end up 150,000 in the red again...?

dialogues.speaker: Nadia
dialogues.text: Ah, congratulations on winning the championship.

choices.text: I still want to go over the shooting challenge...

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: That sounds great. I'd like to take a closer look myself...

choices.text: What are your plans next?

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: Hmm... We still have plenty of funds from Ophelia, so we'll be staying in Snezhnaya a while longer. We'll also pick up some souvenirs for her while we're at it.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: By the way, are you feeling tired, Nadia? Any tiredness or pain?

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: Nope. Following your analysis, it felt as easy as eating a meal — I just enjoyed myself and finished the tournament.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: Well then, since we're talking about food, how about we head to Podvorye Restaurant and order a big feast?

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: Sure! I want... the smoked beetleaf Fish Curls.

response.speaker: Nadia
response.text: I got it yesterday while playing outside — from a little bear. It was delicious.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: Just be careful next time... don't try random things like that.

choices.text: You all did great as well.

response.speaker: Urville
response.text: Thank you for the praise. Nadia had a lot of fun, and I feel even more motivated to train. This tournament was well worth it.

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: So Lan is staying in Snezhnaya a bit longer, hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Sarin
dialogues.text: Let's submit a consultancy fee request to Headquarters for her, just in case.

dialogues.speaker: Valerina
dialogues.text: Snezhnayan cats... are they completely unaffected by the cold?

dialogues.speaker: Talalikhin
dialogues.text: Mm, all the participants are full of enthusiasm... that's a good thing.

dialogues.speaker: Talalikhin
dialogues.text: I just hope they can keep that momentum going after the tournament.

dialogues.speaker: Lemta
dialogues.text: Hmm, that was a satisfying match.

dialogues.speaker: Lemta
dialogues.text: Now that things have calmed down, maybe I should buy some Snezhnayan cosmetics for Avena...

dialogues.speaker: Lemta
dialogues.text: ...Snezhnaya has specialty cosmetics, right?

dialogues.speaker: Sukhrab
dialogues.text: In the end, I didn't even make it onto the rankings...

dialogues.speaker: Sukhrab
dialogues.text: "You've worked hard enough. It's alright."

dialogues.speaker: Sukhrab
dialogues.text: I don't want to hear that from Professor again... At the very least, I need to bring back results that will surprise her.

dialogues.speaker: Match Commentator
dialogues.text: Ugh... I shouted too much. My voice is completely hoarse...

dialogues.speaker: Match Commentator
dialogues.text: The scriptwriter really went overboard... how are we supposed to read this many exclamation marks...?
